definitions.explanation: The act of counting or listing items individually. Almost always appears in the set phrase {枚挙|まいきょ}にいとまがない (too numerous to list).

examples.japanese: {例|れい}は{枚挙|まいきょ}にいとまがない。
examples.english: The examples are too numerous to list.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{功績|こうせき}は{枚挙|まいきょ}にいとまがない。
examples.english: His achievements are too numerous to count.

examples.japanese: {失敗|しっぱい}の{原因|げんいん}は{枚挙|まいきょ}にいとまがないが、{最|もっと}も{大|おお}きいのは{準備|じゅんび}{不足|ぶそく}だった。
examples.english: The causes of the failure are too numerous to list, but the biggest one was insufficient preparation.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost exclusively used in the set phrase {枚挙|まいきょ}にいとまがない (too numerous to enumerate). This is a formal, literary expression meaning there are so many examples, cases, or instances that one could not possibly list them all. The word {暇|いとま} here means "time" or "leisure" — literally, "there is no time to enumerate them all."
This word is rarely used outside of this fixed expression. Learning {枚挙|まいきょ}にいとまがない as a set phrase is the most practical approach.

FIXED PATTERN:
- {枚挙|まいきょ}にいとまがない: too numerous to count/list
